english.title: Evade a prohibition / restriction on the export of goods - other than controlled drug
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were knowingly concerned in the

(A)_[exportation]_
(B)_[attempted exportation]_
(C)_[shipment as stores]_
(D)_[attempted shipment as stores]_

of goods, namely **(..SPECIFY GOODS..), with intent to evade the prohibition or restriction on importation imposed by **(..SPECIFY LEGISLATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 68(2) and (3) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
english.pointstoprove:

english.notes:
(i) For offences committed before 22nd February 2024 refer to H14368.
(ii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Commissioners for Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs, see section 145 of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
(iii) For forfeiture see section 68(5) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
(iv) See H11544 for the equivalent offence applying to the exportation of prohibited weapons / ammunition, with different penalty implications.

consent.description: Commissioners of HM Rev and Customs

other.penalty:
Either way:
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a penalty of three times the value of the goods or a fine not exceeding £20,000 whichever is the greater.
Indictment: maximum 14 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see section 146A of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
